thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: svc-discovery/consul reports elevated SRV failures in region-azc — error-rate 18% over 5m, affected services: auth-proxy, gpu-scheduler. Trigger: service-discovery-srv-failure-rate > 10% :rotating_light:

jamie (oncall): I'm on it. paging received. joining channel.

maria (sre): saw the alert, jumping in. quick check: are these DNS NXDOMAIN or empty SRV responses?

jamie (oncall): initial checks from synthetic probes show many SRV responses empty for service=gpu-scheduler.region-azc. Clients get 502s downstream.

tyler (network): tagging in — I can see increased packet drops between azc kube nodes and consul agents ~17:03 UTC. Could be an AZ-level network flapping event.

elena (support): we have 3 customer escalations for slow job starts and inference timeouts — internal ticket INC-2451 created. Customers: beta-ai, vectra. Noted severity P1 by support.

maria (sre): running quick dig against coredns in azc:
```
; dig +short _gpu-scheduler._tcp.prod.svc.cluster.local SRV @10.10.3.12

; output: (repeatedly returns blank lines)
```

jamie (oncall): consul catalog list for nodes in azc shows some agents offline.

ops-bot: Consul cluster health changed: leader election triggered at 17:04:12 UTC, leader: node-consul-02 -> node-consul-05.

maria (sre): consul members: many CONSUL_SKIP_REFRESH logs and high rpc latency to leader. Might be slow leader responses causing failed SRV lookups. Checking etcd/raft metrics.

tyler (network): confirmed partial network partition for azc->control-plane overlay. Some TCP resets on port 8300/8301 between azc and neighboring AZs. Likely causing consul RPC timeouts.

jamie (oncall): immediate mitigations: (1) divert new deployment traffic away from azc using routing policy until we stabilize, (2) enable fallback to cached SRV set in client-side resolver for 60s, (3) trigger controlled restart of coredns pods in azc after we verify consul agent status.

maria (sre): agreed. I'll validate consul agent health first. Running: `consul operator raft list-peers` and `consul members` from control plane.

maria (sre): output: peer node-consul-05 shows intermittent heartbeat misses; RPC RTT spikes to 2s+; other peers stable. Suspect transient packet loss causing leader election thrash.

tyler (network): network team is applying an AZ fabric patch to the peering route and restoring MTU misconfig that started at ~16:58 UTC. I expect routing reconvergence in ~3-6 minutes. Will update.

elena (support): posting interim customer note: "We're investigating elevated internal service discovery errors in one AZ causing some API timeouts. We have team actively mitigating and will provide updates every 10 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jamie (oncall): patching routing policy now: set route-weight for azc -> 0.2 to drain new traffic. command: `redwood-route update --region azc --weight 0.2 --reason "svc discovery instability"`

ops-bot: route update applied, rollouts underway.

maria (sre): after route drift, SRV failure rate dropped from 18% -> 7% in 2m. Good sign. Still seeing some failed lookups from long-lived clients which cached empty answers.

jamie (oncall): decision: don't restart consul leader until peering stabilizes. We'll restart only coredns pods in azc to clear any hung resolver state. Maria, can you run a rolling restart of coredns with maxUnavailable=1?

maria (sre): starting rolling restart: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns --record` with `kubectl patch deployment/coredns -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"rollingUpdate":{"maxUnavailable":1}}}}'`

maria (sre): post-restart logs show coredns re-established healthy upstream queries to consul agent on localhost. SRV queries now returning expected records.

jamie (oncall): monitoring metrics: SRV failure rate back down to 2% in azc. Client error rates for auth-proxy and gpu-scheduler trending back to baseline.

tyler (network): peering route fix propagated at 17:11 UTC, packet loss normalized. Will continue to monitor for 30m.

elena (support): updated customers with resolution note and ETA for full recovery. Customers reporting improved job starts.

maria (sre): root-cause hypothesis: an AZ peering configuration change earlier caused intermittent MTU/route misconfiguration, which increased RPC latency for consul leading to leader election activity and temporary SRV lookup failures from coredns. The immediate impact was 10-20% increased SRV failures and client timeouts.

jamie (oncall): summary for handoff:
- incident start: 1937205642 (17:02 UTC)
- impact: 2 customer escalations, transient P1s for service startup and inference timeouts in azc. Estimated affected traffic ~6% of platform tokens.
- mitigations applied: routing weight reduction for azc, rolling restart of coredns in azc, network peering MTU fix.
- status: service discovery stability restored, SRV failure rate back to 2%, monitoring green but under 30m watch.

jamie (oncall): handing to maria (secondary) for post-incident follow-up, postmortem, and tie-in with network team's change window. I'm unpaging.

maria (sre): taking handoff. Next actions: collect consul and coredns logs, correlate leadership elections, create postmortem with timeline + action items (1) add automated detection for consul RPC RTT spikes and auto-divert routing, (2) improve client-side SRV cache fallback behavior, (3) validate peering change rollback checklist. Will file PMEM-1937.

tyler (network): I'll add a revert-safe changelog entry for peering config and schedule a post-change verification job.

elena (support): closing INC-2451 once customers confirm no further regression.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: svc-discovery-srv-failure-rate in azc -> normal at 17:24 UTC.

jamie (oncall): thanks team. leaving timeline and evidence in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:

maria (sre): noted — will include query samples, coredns pod logs, consul raft metrics, and packet capture snippets in the postmortem.

ops-bot: Reminder: create RCA ticket and link to this thread.

maria (sre): will do. tagging postmortem owner and setting preliminary severity "major".

elena (support): final customer note draft posted to #customer-notifies for review.

jamie (oncall): night crew: monitor azc SRV metrics for 1h, escalate if >5% sustained.

maria (sre): acknowledged."
